title: PRP injections for joints
what: A little of your blood is taken. A centrifuge separates the plasma with platelets, and it is injected into a joint or tendon.
why: Sometimes for knee arthritis or tendon and ligament problems. It does not help everyone. Talk with your doctor about whether it suits you.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes; the effect, if any, shows after a few weeks; a course is often needed
tell_doctor: Blood thinners and anti-inflammatory pills. Your doctor will decide what to do
If you have an infection or fever now
If you had injections in this joint before

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: You are sometimes asked to stop anti-inflammatory pills for a few days before and after. Do not stop them on your own. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat light, without fatty food, and drink water. This gives better plasma.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, so the joint is easy to uncover.

steps: Blood is taken from a vein, like a blood test
The tube is spun in a centrifuge for a few minutes
The skin over the joint is cleaned with antiseptic
The doctor injects the plasma into the joint with a needle, often guided by ultrasound
feel: A prick when blood is taken and when the injection is given
A feeling of fullness in the joint
Pain and swelling in the joint for 1 to 3 days after are common
after: For the first few days, avoid putting heavy strain on the joint
Cold on the joint is fine if it hurts. Anti-inflammatory pills only if your doctor advises
Your doctor will decide on repeat injections
red_flags: The joint is hot, very swollen, and painful, or you have a fever over 38°C (100.4°F): see a doctor right away
Pain gets much worse after 2 to 3 days

faq.a: Not for everyone. For some people the pain gets better, for others the effect is weak. Your doctor will say whether it makes sense for you.

faq.q: Can I be allergic to my own plasma?
faq.a: An allergy to your own plasma is unlikely. But pain and swelling in the joint after the injection can happen.

reminders.text: PRP tomorrow. Drink water today and in the morning, and eat light. Follow your doctor's advice on anti-inflammatory pills.
